scope: KernelLedger implemented UI candidates, change-focused criteria; scores are not interchangeable with earlier Marimo-review averages.

scores.label: Visual consistency
scores.why: Grok gives resting/success/error cells a consistent container and stronger failure boundary. Sol is quieter, with more open canvas.

scores.label: Text readability
scores.why: Both preserve the 14 px editor default and approximately 21 px code pitch; no evidence of a new font-size advantage.

scores.label: Notebook identification
scores.why: Sol shows the full fixture name at the roomy size. Grok retains middle ellipsis there; both improve path context and suffix discovery over baseline.

scores.label: Navigation / Run clarity
scores.why: Both keep Run all labeled at 800 and secondary destinations reachable. Sol uses a current-destination dropdown; Grok adds an explicit Views menu.

scores.label: Compact vertical space
scores.why: Both reduce the defined source/output extent from 204 to 172 logical px (15.7%), with matched content and typography.

scores.label: Editor horizontal space
scores.why: At 1280 the editable rectangle shrinks from 964 logical px to 760 in Sol and 788 in Grok. Grok is 28 px wider; both sacrifice room to gutters/action columns.

scores.label: Responsive / large text
scores.why: Both pass the 800-wide header checks. At UI scale 2 with 24 px code, Sol uses a wider header fallback; Grok keeps the gutter and wraps substantially more source.

scores.label: Error presentation
scores.why: Both preserve readable summaries/disclosure and wrap the tested traceback. Grok adds a coherent danger border/rail and explicit alert icon.

scores.label: Keyboard / access evidence
scores.why: Both pass contextual focus/menu return and expose Markdown names. Sol provides a document/heading structure; footer/save-state exposure remains incomplete or unverified in both.

scores.label: Execution feedback
scores.why: Both retain Ready/Saved/outcomes and offer off-by-default recorded durations verified after rerun. No startup-speed, live-queue or memory ranking is implied.

qualification: Native automated journeys, UIA patterns and headless tests; no Narrator/NVDA qualification or user study; no performance ranking.
